messages.text:
Ok, PR 100 is merged.



Now, let us establish the baseline Tracking performance of the ODD, using ACTS truth tracking

- both Geant4 and Fatras simulation
- material maps as of PR #100 and ACTS Gen-3 geometry 
- single muons 1, 10, 100 GeV transverse momentum,
- Digitization:
  - geometric pixel: RD53 50 um x 50 um
  - geometric short strips: defaults as of module design
  - geometric long strips: defaults as of module design
- the performance should show resolutions, pulls versus eta and pT using a full_chain_odd.py equivalent with truth tracking first

I’ll check the merged material map, ACTS Gen-3 setup and module digitization defaults, then establish a reproducible truth-tracking baseline for Geant4 and Fatras at 1, 10 and 100 GeV pT. I’ll use the nODD coordination and validation workflows and the `acts-spack` skill to verify the native environment before running.

The Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so I’ll recheck the runtime directly. I’m treating “ODD” here as the Gen-3 tracker used in PR #100, keeping the geometry and material-map IDs matched. I’ll also read the strip pitches and stereo angles from the module designs.

Which magnetic field should this first tracking baseline use? The ACTS ODD full-chain example uses a constant 2 T field; the nODD solenoid proposal has a 3 T central field but is not yet installed in the tracking geometry. I’ll use constant 2 T if you have no preference.
- Constant 2 T, matching the ODD example
- Constant 3 T, as an ideal-field nODD baseline
- The finite DES-026 solenoid field

The runtime imports succeed, and Geant4 11.4.3 reports all 12 datasets installed. The module defaults are **75 µm × 0.5 mm short-strip cells** and **80 µm single-coordinate long strips**, with stereo supplied by the two physical sensor faces. Pixels will use the requested **50 µm × 50 µm** cells.

I’ll start with 20,000 single-muon events per momentum and backend, uniform in η and φ, and retain fit failures alongside the resolution and pull plots.

SoftEng is implementing the native chain and testing both simulation backends. I’m preparing the performance analysis in parallel: perigee residuals and pulls, relative pT resolution, and counts showing losses before and during fitting. The report will distinguish truth-associated fitting from pattern-recognition performance.

I’ll use a **constant 3 T field** for both simulation and fitting, recorded as an ideal-field nODD baseline.

The first **3 T Fatras pilot** completed: all 100 muons produced fitted tracks, with no invalid covariance reported. The exact 65-portal, 8,550-bin map reload passed. Geant4 is now running its pilot; I’ll check its hit IDs and digitization coverage before accepting production results.

The pilots caught two configuration problems before production: Geant4’s default material-name list omitted `pixel_Silicon`, and long-strip digitization needs a physical along-strip bin even though it measures only one coordinate. SoftEng is correcting both and retaining the earlier pilots as excluded controls.
